rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Setup 3 Gameplay 4 End of Game 5 Variants 5.1 Tiebreakers 5.2 Discard Pile Objective The more meerkats (and their points) you collected, the better. But be careful for the vultures! Setup Each player takes a set of 1-15 cards. Shuffle the 15 point cards (vultures and meerkats) and put them face down. Gameplay The game consists of 15 rounds. In each round, first turn over a point card. Each player choose a card to play, face down. Then everyone reveal their cards at once. All ties are ignored, then if the card (or the sum) is a meerkat it goes to the highest player, lowest if vulture. If there are only ties, nobody gets it. It will be bided with the next card. All players set aside the cards they played in their discard piles. Any player can consult any discard pile at any time. Meerkat values 1 to 10 Vulture values -1 to -5 End of Game After 15 rounds, the game ends. All remaining point cards in the middle are discarded. All players add up their scores. Meerkats are positively scored while vultures are negatively scored. The player with the highest score wins. Variants Tiebreakers Basic rules: If there is a tie, all tied players lose and the player with the next untied score wins. Meerkat tiebreaker: If there is a tie, the tied player with the highest-valued meerkat card wins. Discard Pile Discard visible: You can see the discard piles of each player. Last card visible: You can see the last card played by each player.

[Rating: 3/10] Just a simple guessing game.  You bid on tiles with points -5 to 10 (excluding 0), using cards with values of 1 to 15 in your hand.  When all tiles have been bid for the game is over.  Like I said - a pure guessing game with out any meat whatsoever.  No real tactics or strategy.

[Rating: 3/10] The simplicity, brevity, and elegance of the game are appealing factors which I can appreciate, but I dislike it since you can win by playing in a totally arbitrary fashion.

[Rating: 3/10] No real skill involved. Players can play cards at random and still have a shot at winning.

[Rating: 3/10] Very chaotic blind selection of cards.  Sure some may say that if you watch the cards and apply probabilities you can "guess" your opponents play.  If you can do that, go play Blackjack or Poker.

[Rating: 3/10] This is not really a game. It's nothing like what I expected, and the only use I've been able to find for it is to determine who plays first in a real game. Very disappointing.
